statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-70159 (GHSA-334f-vvp4-7g6p) is an ASP.NET Core SignalR denial of service issue: stateful reconnect clients can block broadcasts indefinitely through MessageBuffer.ResendAsync backpressure and keep the associated resources alive. Microsoft lists Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Common as affected from 9.0.0 through 9.0.20 and fixed in 9.0.21, names Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Core as the other affected library, and lists Windows, Linux and macOS as affected platforms (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-334f-vvp4-7g6p, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/452, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.21/9.0.21.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. Implementation copies of Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Common.dll and Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Core.dll are in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App shared framework (aspnetcore9-runtime, and the .NET SDK held by dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap) and in the ASP.NET Core runtime pack in dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap, and SignalR.Common is also in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Common nupkg in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts. Every implementation copy carries the build's own .NET version, so the copies in the first 8 builds (9.0.12-r0 to 9.0.20-r0) are unfixed and every copy from 9.0.21-r0 on is 9.0.21 or later; the other copies are reference assemblies with no implementation code. The range ends at 9.0.21-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
